hook.text: A downburst is a powerful downdraft that hits the ground and spreads out—producing winds rivaling weak tornadoes.

buildup.text: Rain evaporating in dry air below the storm cools the air, making it denser—gravity accelerates it downward.

discovery.text: Microbursts concentrate this energy over a small area, with winds that can exceed 240 km/h.

twist.text: Microbursts are extremely dangerous to aircraft—several fatal crashes were caused by unexpected wind shear on landing.

climax.text: After disasters in the 1980s, airports installed LLWAS systems and training programs to detect and avoid microbursts.

punchline.text: Invisible wind from above—one of aviation's deadliest foes.

quiz.question: What causes a microburst?
options: Intense concentrated downdraft spreading at the surface
